1. 
The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been cheating by Somraj Saha and Ayush Virmani in selling the car to the petitioner without disclosing that the State Bank of India has not issued a 'no due certificate'.
The petitioner proceeds on the basis that all the EMIs under the hypothecation would be duly paid by the seller.
2. The learned Counsel for the State produces the case diary and submits that the petitioner has not complied with the notice under Section 41A of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

Accordingly, we direct that in the event of arrest the petitioner namely, Sudhangsu Sarkar, shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-, with two sureties of like amount each,
one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of Arresting Officer and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the petitioner shall meet the I.O. once in a week till the submission of final report.

The petitioner shall appear before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Alipore, South 24 Parganas, in connection with S.L. Case No. 61 of 2024,
within two weeks from date.
